summary: Clay Lookout Tower in Clay County, GA, is on a Georgia tower list with coordinates and codes; no source found on its build, staffing, status or site today.

evidence.supports: Tower list entry: Clay Lookout Tower, county Clay, coordinates, reference codes BLL-41130 and gfc-203
Page says its map shows Georgia fire towers, which is the basis for calling Clay Lookout Tower a fire lookout
evidence.quote: Map shows GA fire towers listed by USGS name database (1-72)

evidence.supports: Page carries a revision stamp dated 22 March 2016 (a Google-map revision line); it is not stated to date the list itself
Georgia's fire towers are called iconic and quite endangered
evidence.quote: Georgia’s iconic fire towers are actually quite endangered.

evidence.supports: Georgia Forestry Commission began phasing out tower operators in the late 1980s in favor of an air patrol system
evidence.quote: In the late 1980s, the Georgia Forestry Commission began phasing out the tower operators in favor of an air patrol system.

evidence.supports: Many towers were scrapped and sold; some of those remaining are used when air service is unavailable
evidence.quote: Many were scrapped and sold and of the ones that remain, some are used when air service is unavailable.

notes_for_editor: Only one tower-specific record was found: the tnlandforms.us Georgia list (GA016), which matches the brief's coordinates, county and BLL-41130 / gfc-203 codes. No source reached gives a build year, builder, staffing, fires, status, access or a description of the site today, so the story is short and the events list is empty. The list states no unit for its elevation column (421; the brief's 128.3 m equals 421 ft). The list does not explain what the BLL and gfc codes mean; gfc-203 may point to Georgia Forestry Commission records, but that is unconfirmed. The NHLR Georgia list (http://nhlr.org/lookouts/us/ga/, 29 entries) does not include a Clay tower, so NHLR is not a register for this tower. Lead to check: the Vanishing Georgia photo essay titled 'Fire Tower, Clay County' may show this tower, but its text names no tower or location. The same list also has a second Clay County tower, GA043 Perkins Lookout Tower (31.75100,-84.99243), so the photo could be of either. Next steps: GFC fire-tower records or the code key for BLL and gfc; Clay County newspapers for the tower's construction and removal; a verified photo caption.
